items.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
items.summary: We’re giving developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers access to Gemini 4 Argon, our latest frontier model.

items.title: Introducing the Amazon Bedrock Trusted Access API, with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and Enterprise Data Controls for Claude models
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock now offers a trusted access program API: one place to discover, request, and enroll in model provider programs. The first two offerings, in public preview, are Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) and Enterprise Data Controls (EDC), which give you control over your data when you use Claude Fable models.

items.title: Meta ads is now available in AWS Quick
items.summary: AWS Quick now has a Meta ads AI connector. Meta advertisers can use natural language in Quick to create, manage, and analyze campaigns while staying connected to the Meta ad management network, and combine Meta ad data with first- and third-party sources to build dashboards, documents, slide decks, and automated workflows.

items.title: New in AWS Quick: More capable flows, an updated web experience, and agents that work together
items.summary: AWS Quick is the AI workspace built only for work. Today we’re releasing updates that help your team get more done: build and run business-process flows in chat, triage your day in the updated web app, get more complete answers from multiple agents at once, and connect new data sources like Meta ads and Amplitude.

items.title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill
items.summary: Self-hosting LLMs on GPUs means paying to recompute the same context on every turn. Distributed KV caching with Amazon ElastiCache can cut inference cost by up to 40% and time to first token by up to 80%. This post walks through the distributed KV caching skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS, which evaluates and sets up the cache from your coding agent.

items.title: Introducing managed cluster extensions for observability and user management in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Slurm
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers managed cluster extensions for observability and user management, bringing declarative, API- and console-driven configuration to the software running on Slurm cluster nodes. This post explains how the extensions work and follows a platform team through a quarter of running a shared Slurm cluster with them.

items.title: Introducing Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Global Inference Gateway: One endpoint across Regions and clusters
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod introduces the Global Inference Gateway, one managed endpoint that routes inference requests across your HyperPod clusters in one Region or across Regions. It picks the best cluster, fails over automatically, and authenticates every request with SigV4 and IAM over AWS PrivateLink.

items.title: How Standard Bank Group automates AI risk assessment for generative AI
items.summary: Standard Bank Group automated the evidence behind its generative AI approval gates. Working with AWS Professional Services, the bank built an assessment in its own AWS account that scores each use case against international AI standards and its own policies using LLM-as-a-judge on Amazon Bedrock, giving risk committees consistent, traceable evidence.

items.title: Announcing Amazon Textract Insights: Verifiable generative AI for documents
items.summary: Announcing the general availability of Amazon Textract Insights, a new generative AI feature of Amazon Textract. Describe the fields you need in natural language, submit a document or a mixed packet, and receive structured results with a confidence score and page-level grounding for each value, with no model training required.

items.title: Introducing enhanced infrastructure observability in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now offers enhanced observability to help you diagnose GPU training issues faster. It brings together diagnostic and profiling capabilities for training workloads on both Amazon EKS and Slurm orchestrators, pinpointing issues across GPU, network, and host layers.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Inference: 2026 launches in review, part 2
items.summary: This second installment reviews 13 more Amazon SageMaker AI inference launches from 2026, spanning configuration recommendations, fitting more models onto each GPU, serving models too large for one instance, cross-Region routing, and post-launch tuning, bringing the year’s total to 26.
